annotations.title: Bridge quote (XRP <-> Bitcoin, BNB Chain, Base)

description: FREE. Get a live, firm quote to move funds both ways between native XRP on the XRP Ledger and BTC on Bitcoin, BNB, USDT or USDC on BNB Chain (bsc), or USDC or ETH on Base (12 live routes). Returns quote_id, exact payment instructions (amount, asset, network, pay_to, expiry), the N9T2 fee (1.45 XRP equivalent) and the estimated destination amount. Creating a quote moves no funds. Optional source_amount up to 1000 USDC / 1500 XRP / 0.5 ETH / 1.5 BNB / 1000 USDT / 0.02 BTC; larger transfers go to the OTC desk (boss@n9t2.com). Next: customer approves and pays in their own wallet, then call n9t2_bridge_submit_payment.

destination_address.description: Customer-controlled destination wallet: r... classic address for xrpl, bc1.../3.../1... for bitcoin, 0x... for bsc or base.
destination_address.title: Destination Address

destination_asset.description: Asset delivered: XRP on xrpl; BTC on bitcoin; BNB, USDT or USDC on bsc; USDC or ETH on base.
destination_asset.title: Destination Asset

destination_chain.description: Chain that receives the funds; must differ from source_chain, and one of the two must be xrpl.
destination_chain.title: Destination Chain

source_amount.description: Optional amount to bridge in the source asset as a decimal string, e.g. '250'. The N9T2 fee is added on top. Self-serve cap: 1000 USDC, 1500 XRP, 0.5 ETH, 1.5 BNB, 1000 USDT or 0.02 BTC. Omit for the live route minimum.
source_amount.title: Source Amount

source_asset.description: Asset the customer pays with: XRP on xrpl; BTC on bitcoin; BNB, USDT or USDC on bsc; USDC or ETH on base.
source_asset.title: Source Asset

source_chain.description: Chain the customer pays from: xrpl (XRP Ledger), bitcoin, bsc (BNB Chain) or base. Every route has xrpl on one side.
source_chain.title: Source Chain

name: n9t2_bridge_quote

description: FREE. Read the immutable, customer-safe receipt for a bridge transfer by quote_id: status, amount paid, amount delivered, N9T2 fee, route cost and the payment and delivery transaction hashes. A transfer is complete only when status is 'settled' and settlement.status is 'completed'. 404 means not ready yet.

quote_id.description: quote_id of the transfer to check.
quote_id.title: Quote Id

name: n9t2_bridge_receipt

description: FREE. Submit the transaction hash of the customer's real payment for a bridge quote. N9T2 verifies it on-chain against the quote (exact amount, asset, recipient, expiry) and, once verified, executes the cross-chain delivery through its exactly-once worker. Resubmitting the same quote_id and hash returns the existing record. Verification is not completion: follow up with n9t2_bridge_receipt.

transaction_hash.description: Hash of the customer's actual source-chain payment for that quote. Never a planned or fabricated hash.
transaction_hash.title: Transaction Hash

name: n9t2_bridge_submit_payment

description: Read-only XRPL payment-path discovery for planning a Payment from source_account to destination_account. destination_amount is the exact amount the destination should receive, provided as XRP drops or an issued-currency object; the result returns candidate path alternatives and source-amount information to compare before constructing the payment. Use this when XRPL routing is needed between the source and destination accounts; use n9t2_xrpl_get_book_offers for DEX order-book depth instead. This tool only discovers paths and does not construct, sign, submit, or modify any XRPL transaction; after selecting a route, use n9t2_xrpl_prepare_transaction to build the unsigned payment.

destination_account.description: XRPL classic account address that will receive the destination amount.
destination_account.title: Destination Account

destination_amount.description: Destination amount to deliver. Use a string for XRP drops or an issued-currency object containing currency, issuer, and value.
destination_amount.title: Destination Amount

source_account.description: XRPL classic account address used as the source of payment-path discovery.
source_account.title: Source Account

name: n9t2_xrpl_find_path

description: Read-only XRPL current-account-state lookup for one account. `account` must be a valid XRPL classic account address; the result returns the current balance, sequence, owner count, flags, and account settings without submitting or modifying any XRPL transaction, and calls remain subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for current account state only; use n9t2_xrpl_get_transaction or n9t2_xrpl_list_account_transactions for transaction history, and n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger_data for raw ledger objects.

account.description: XRPL classic account address whose current account state should be retrieved.
account.title: Account

name: n9t2_xrpl_get_account_info

description: Read-only XRPL Automated Market Maker (AMM) state lookup for a specific pool. Identify the pool with `amm_account`, or with the paired `asset` and `asset2` currency objects; `account` is optional context used by the native AMM lookup when applicable. Use `ledger_hash` or `ledger_index` to pin the lookup to a specific ledger. The result returns native `amm_info` data including pool balances, LP token supply, trading fee, auction slot, and vote slots when present. This paid lookup does not modify the ledger and is subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for AMM pool state; use n9t2_xrpl_get_book_offers for DEX order-book depth and n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger_data for raw ledger-state objects.

account.description: Optional XRPL account used by the native AMM lookup when applicable.
account.title: Account

amm_account.description: Optional AMM account address identifying the specific AMM ledger object.
amm_account.title: Amm Account

asset.description: First AMM asset specification using an XRPL currency object.
asset.title: Asset

asset2.description: Second AMM asset specification paired with asset.
asset2.title: Asset2

ledger_hash.description: Optional ledger hash used to pin the AMM lookup to a specific ledger.
ledger_hash.title: Ledger Hash

ledger_index.description: Optional ledger index or selector used to pin the lookup to a specific ledger.
ledger_index.title: Ledger Index

name: n9t2_xrpl_get_amm_info

description: Read-only XRPL DEX order-book lookup for a specific trading pair. `taker_gets` and `taker_pays` are the required XRPL currency-specification objects that define the two sides of the book; `limit` optionally caps the number of offers returned. The result provides global book offers and market-depth data without modifying the ledger, and calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for global DEX order-book depth; use n9t2_xrpl_list_account_offers for one account's outstanding offers and n9t2_xrpl_find_path when you need payment-path discovery instead.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of DEX order-book offers to return.
limit.title: Limit

taker_gets.description: Currency specification for the asset the taker receives in the XRPL DEX order book.
taker_gets.title: Taker Gets

taker_pays.description: Currency specification for the asset the taker pays in the XRPL DEX order book.
taker_pays.title: Taker Pays

name: n9t2_xrpl_get_book_offers

description: Read-only XRPL issued-asset exposure calculation for one issuing account. `account` is the required XRPL issuer address; optionally use `hotwallet` with one address or a list of operational hot-wallet addresses when those balances should be included in the calculation, and use `ledger_index` to pin the calculation to a specific ledger. `strict` controls how account identifiers are interpreted. The result reports the calculated issued-asset exposure without modifying the ledger, and calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for issuer-level issued-asset exposure; do not use it for trust-line holdings of a single account, where n9t2_xrpl_list_account_lines is the appropriate tool.

account.description: XRPL issuing account whose issued-asset balances should be calculated.
account.title: Account

hotwallet.description: Optional XRPL hot-wallet account address or list of hot-wallet addresses.
hotwallet.title: Hotwallet

ledger_index.description: Optional ledger index or selector for the balance calculation.
ledger_index.title: Ledger Index

strict.description: Whether account identifiers should be interpreted strictly as supplied.
strict.title: Strict

name: n9t2_xrpl_get_gateway_balances

description: Read-only XRPL ledger header and metadata lookup. Omit `ledger_index` to use the current validated ledger, or provide a validated ledger index/selector to pin the lookup; set `transactions=true` to include that ledger's transactions and use `expand=true` to return those transactions as full objects. The result provides ledger metadata and, when requested, transaction data without modifying the ledger, and calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for ledger headers, metadata, and optional ledger transactions; use n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger_data instead when you need raw ledger-state objects.

expand.description: Whether returned transactions should be expanded into full transaction objects.
expand.title: Expand

ledger_index.description: Optional validated ledger index or ledger selector. Omit to use the current validated ledger.
ledger_index.title: Ledger Index

transactions.description: Whether to include transactions contained in the requested ledger.
transactions.title: Transactions

name: n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger

description: Read-only XRPL raw ledger-state lookup for a ledger. Omit `ledger_index` to use the default ledger, or provide a ledger index/selector to pin the lookup; use `limit` to cap the number of ledger-state objects returned and pass `marker` from a previous response to continue pagination. The result returns raw canonical ledger-state entries without modifying the ledger; large state queries should be paginated, and calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for canonical ledger-state objects; use n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger for ledger headers and transaction-list metadata instead.

ledger_index.description: Optional ledger index or selector identifying the ledger whose state objects should be returned.
ledger_index.title: Ledger Index

limit.description: Optional maximum number of ledger-state objects to return.
limit.title: Limit

marker.description: Pagination marker returned by a previous response.
marker.title: Marker

name: n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger_data

description: Read-only XRPL `server_info` lookup for node health, server state, and validated-ledger status. Use this before interpreting ledger-dependent results when node health or freshness matters; the result provides the node/server status and validated-ledger information needed to assess whether subsequent ledger reads are current and usable. Use n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger for ledger metadata or n9t2_xrpl_get_ledger_data for raw ledger-state entries; this tool requires no parameters and does not modify the ledger.
name: n9t2_xrpl_get_server_info

description: Read-only XRPL transaction lookup for one canonical transaction hash. `transaction` is the required hash; set `binary=true` only when binary-encoded transaction data is required, otherwise use the normal transaction representation. The result retrieves transaction data for that hash without modifying the ledger, and calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this when the transaction hash is already known; use n9t2_xrpl_list_account_transactions for account-wide transaction history instead.

binary.description: Whether to return the transaction in binary encoded form.
binary.title: Binary

transaction.description: Canonical XRPL transaction hash to retrieve.
transaction.title: Transaction

name: n9t2_xrpl_get_transaction

description: Read-only XRPL Payment Channel lookup for one account. `account` is the required XRPL classic account address; by default, the lookup returns channels where that account is the source. Use `destination_account` to filter channels by destination, `ledger_index` to pin the lookup to a validated ledger, and `marker` to continue pagination; `limit` caps returned channels and defaults to 200. The result lists Payment Channel entries without modifying the ledger, and calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for PaymentChannelCreate/Fund/Claim inspection; use n9t2_xrpl_list_account_objects for generic account ledger objects instead.

The result lists trust-line state including issued-asset balances and limits without modifying the ledger, and calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for an account's trust lines and issued-asset holdings; use n9t2_xrpl_get_account_info for current account state or n9t2_xrpl_list_account_objects for other ledger objects.

description: Read-only XRPL NFT inventory lookup for one classic account using the native `account_nfts` method. The result provides NFT-specific fields such as `NFTokenID`, `Issuer`, `NFTokenTaxon`, `URI`, and `nft_serial`; use `marker` to continue pagination and `ledger_hash` or `ledger_index` to pin the inventory lookup to a specific ledger. Calls are subject to the configured gateway rate limits. Use this for NFTs owned by an account; use n9t2_xrpl_list_nft_offers for marketplace buy/sell offers on a specific NFTokenID, or n9t2_xrpl_list_account_objects when raw account ledger objects rather than NFT-specific fields are required.

Set object_type to `nft_offer` only when raw NFTokenOffer ledger entries are required; use `ledger_index` to pin the lookup and `limit`/`marker` for pagination.

description: Prepare one unsigned XRPL transaction for agent-local signing. Choose exactly one transaction_type and provide that transaction model's fields in parameters; unsupported transaction types or invalid builder parameters are rejected before an unsigned transaction is returned. Sequence, fee, and last_ledger_sequence may be autofilled when omitted. The result is unsigned transaction JSON for local signing; after signing, pass the signed tx_blob to n9t2_xrpl_submit_transaction. N9T2 never receives or stores private keys, seeds, or wallet secrets. Use this as the generic transaction-construction primitive for supported XRPL transaction types, including Payment, TrustSet, OfferCreate, and OfferCancel.

parameters.description: Typed XRPL transaction fields used to build the unsigned transaction. Sequence, fee, and last_ledger_sequence may be autofilled when omitted.
parameters.title: Parameters

transaction_type.description: XRPL transaction model name to prepare, selected from the supported transaction types advertised by this tool.
transaction_type.title: Transaction Type

name: n9t2_xrpl_prepare_transaction

description: Submit one already-signed XRPL transaction to the network. `tx_blob` must be the complete signed transaction encoded as hexadecimal; obtain it from the caller's local signing step, normally after `n9t2_xrpl_prepare_transaction`. This action mutates ledger state when the transaction is accepted into the XRPL network and must never receive private keys, seeds, or wallet secrets. `fail_hard` forwards rippled's option and defaults to false; when true, a transaction that fails locally is not retried or relayed. The result preserves the raw submit response, including `engine_result` and `engine_result_message` and, when returned, `accepted`, `queued`, `validated`, and transaction data. Submission is tentative; use `n9t2_xrpl_get_transaction` with the returned transaction hash to confirm validated-ledger inclusion. Invalid hexadecimal or XRPL-rejected blobs return an error.

fail_hard.description: Forward rippled's fail_hard option. When true, a transaction that fails locally is not retried or relayed to other servers. Defaults to false.
fail_hard.title: Fail Hard

tx_blob.description: Complete signed XRPL transaction encoded as hexadecimal. The caller must sign locally before sending it to N9T2.
tx_blob.title: Tx Blob

name: n9t2_xrpl_submit_transaction

custody.description: Non-custodial confirmation. N9T2 never receives, stores, or uses the caller's private keys, seeds, or wallet secrets.
custody.title: Custody

signed_blob_submitted.description: True when the validated hexadecimal tx_blob was forwarded to the XRPL submit method.
signed_blob_submitted.title: Signed Blob Submitted

submission.description: Raw XRPL rippled submit response. Inspect engine_result and engine_result_message for the tentative submission outcome; the response may also include accepted, queued, validated, tx_json, and other XRPL submission fields.
submission.title: Submission

description: Open a bounded native XRPL WebSocket subscription and capture live events for selected streams, accounts, proposed transactions, or order books. Use this when an agent needs event-driven updates instead of a one-time snapshot. The tool sends the XRPL subscribe command, collects events until duration_seconds expires or max_events is reached, then closes the connection and returns the subscription acknowledgement plus captured events. When subscription inputs are omitted, the default is the ledger stream for 3 seconds with up to 25 events. This is read-only: it does not submit transactions or modify ledger state. Do not request the admin-only peer_status stream unless the upstream XRPL server permits it.

accounts.description: Optional list of XRPL classic account addresses whose activity should be streamed.
accounts.title: Accounts

accounts_proposed.description: Optional list of XRPL accounts for proposed transaction events.
accounts_proposed.title: Accounts Proposed

books.description: Optional list of XRPL order-book subscription descriptors.
books.title: Books

duration_seconds.description: How many seconds the bounded WebSocket subscription remains open. Default is 3.
duration_seconds.title: Duration Seconds

max_events.description: Maximum number of events to capture before returning. Default is 25.
max_events.title: Max Events

streams.description: Optional XRPL stream names such as ledger or transactions.
streams.title: Streams

name: n9t2_xrpl_subscribe
